_comment: Fixture assets. Every entry must carry licence and source: these files ship inside client deliverables. CC0 is required - an attribution obligation discovered late in a client proposal is expensive. Textures are stripped deliberately; geometry is what the parametric recipes cannot supply, and a source asset's own finish is neither neutral nor appropriate to a retail interior. Seating carries seat_height_mm as well as overall height: retail schedules quote seat height for chairs and stools, so comparing a declared height against an asset's overall height compares two different measurements and wrongly rejects a good match. ONE documented exception to the no-textures rule: product_phone_generic -- see its own 'texture_exception' field for why.

stool.author: Dairon Sanchez
stool.modifications: Re-decimated from the original 14,373-triangle source (source textures removed, flat grey vertex colour applied to match the original). Replaces an earlier ~3000-triangle decimation that visibly broke the thin footrest ring and seat rim -- render-only artifact under Cycles (flickering, not a crash or an export failure), reproduced identically regardless of decimation algorithm (Blender's own modifier and trimesh's quadric decimation both did it), and confirmed to onset specifically between roughly 7,000 and 9,000 triangles for this mesh's thin round geometry. 9,000 is the lowest tested count that renders clean; instance count per store is low (a handful of stools, not hundreds), so the larger file cost is worth it over shipping a visibly broken asset.

chair.author: Ethan Place
chair.modifications: decimated to ~3000 triangles; source textures removed

pillar.author: Kenney
pillar.modifications: source textures removed (already low-poly, no decimation needed)
pillar.style_note: plain square column with a simple pyramidal cap -- checked visually before integration. A same-search Quaternius 'Column' candidate (poly.pizza/m/wLubNpOTX4) was rejected despite matching license and rough dimensions: rendered inspection showed an ornate fluted classical column with a decorative capital, wrong for a modern retail interior. Dimension and license checks alone did not catch that; only looking at it did.

product_phone_generic.author: Brian MacIntosh (BMacZero)
product_phone_generic.licence_verified: Stated directly on the asset page as CC0; author explicitly removed the original trademarked branding after community feedback, before this manifest entry was written -- 'redacted' in the shipped texture's own filename.
product_phone_generic.texture_exception: Textures are stripped on every other asset in this manifest (see the top-level comment) because geometry is what a parametric recipe cannot supply and a source finish is not neutral. This asset is the deliberate exception: it is a small product prop whose entire identifying read -- screen, camera dot, nav buttons -- is baked into a 300-triangle mesh's diffuse texture, not modelled as geometry. Stripping it would leave a plain rounded slab, which is exactly what the existing procedural device_body/device_screen bands already build (see fixture_types.py) -- i.e. it would make using an external asset here pointless. Texture kept, on purpose, for this asset only.
product_phone_generic.modifications: Original OBJ had no linked material (broken mtllib reference on download); re-attached the asset's own already-redacted texture and re-exported as GLB. Texture resized 1024x1024 -> 512x512 and re-encoded JPEG q85 (20KB) -- the same size/format discipline as the floor/wall textures in app/assets/textures/ -- since this asset is placed many times per fixture (a shelf/table full of product) and trimesh does not instance geometry (see mesh_builder.py's known GLB-instancing limitation): every placed copy embeds its own geometry, so the shared texture must stay small. No decimation needed; already low-poly.
product_phone_generic.usage_note: Placed procedurally by mesh_builder's per-cell asset placement (Band.asset_key on wall_bay's stock_N and island_table's device bands), not through the whole-fixture fit_asset ladder used for chair/stool/pillar -- see mesh_builder.py's _place_prop_in_cell. Scaled to a fixed target size per placement context, not to a declared BOQ dimension, since this represents anonymous shelf/table product, not a scheduled fixture.
product_phone_generic.not_representative: Modelled after a real 2008-era compact slider phone (visible in the model's own filename before redaction), reused here purely as a generic silhouette+screen stand-in. It is not, and is not meant to be, a real client product model -- see PLANFORGE.md / the client asset request for why a real one is not available yet.

product_laptop_generic.native_pose_reason: An open laptop has no thin axis to stand on the way a phone or chair does -- it is physically an L-shape (base + raised screen), not a slab. Normalised already resting in its natural open-on-a-table pose (screen up) rather than forced into the manifest's default standing convention; see asset_loader.native_pose.
product_laptop_generic.author: Kenney
product_laptop_generic.licence_verified: Public Domain (CC0) badge on the model's own Poly Pizza page, same author already used for pillar.glb -- Kenney publishes everything as CC0 (kenney.nl states this site-wide), no login required to download.
product_laptop_generic.modifications: The downloaded GLB contained the entire model duplicated wholesale as two fully-overlapping copies (6 mesh nodes reducing to 3 once deduplicated by identical world-space bounds) -- an export artifact, not a deliberate LOD/variant (confirmed: every duplicate pair shares exact vertex data and an identical transform). Rebuilt via trimesh keeping one copy of each of the 3 parts, each baked to flat ColorVisuals vertex colours from its original PBR baseColorFactor (the source has no texture to strip -- flat-shaded already, same as chair.glb/stool.glb). Re-exported as GLB; halved the vertex/face count with no visible change.
product_laptop_generic.usage_note: Placed procedurally by mesh_builder's per-cell asset placement (see product_phone_generic's own usage_note for the mechanism), widening wall_bay/island_table's product catalog beyond a single phone silhouette -- see visual_profiles.py's product_catalog. A ColorVisuals asset (no embedded texture), unlike product_phone_generic -- _place_prop_in_cell handles both, see its is_textured branch.
